content:
You will meet people who already belong to a church. A Core Group member names three families from their congregation. A neighbor asks whether you are looking for people. A list starts to look like the easy way to fill the next Vision Meeting.

If you plan to recruit members of a congregation, agree on sending with that church's leaders before you invite. That order is for this kind of recruitment. It is not a rule that a pastor may permit or refuse someone's departure. Everyfield does not certify that choice, and it does not gate it.

---

## Agree before you build the list

Targeted recruitment means you are choosing people because they belong to that church, or you are asking your Core Group to work that membership. A sending arrangement is what you and that church's leaders agree before any of those invitations go out. Name the purpose, who may invite, and what you will do if the leaders decline.

Talk with the pastor or the other leaders who can speak for the congregation. A side chat with a friend on staff is not the agreement. If someone else shepherds those members week to week, include the leader who would otherwise hear about the invitations secondhand.

<Callout type="important">
Agreeing on sending is a conversation between people. Everyfield does not judge calling, character, fitness, or spiritual health. It does not give another pastor a vote or a view of your people records. Belonging to a church or a network is not access to those records.
</Callout>

---

## Two different conversations

Planned recruitment and a personal ask are different. Treat them as the same and you will either hand another pastor a veto or turn one person's interest into a campaign.

| Situation | What you do |
| --- | --- |
| You plan to invite current members of one congregation | Pause. Agree on sending with that church's leaders first. |
| Someone independently asks to visit or to join | Hear them. Their pastor's permission is not required. |
| A former connection, already gone from that church | Invite them directly. You are not recruiting an active membership. |
| Someone reports harm, or contact would be unsafe | Do not send their story to that church as a recruitment step. |

[Growing Your Core Group](/wiki/core-group/building-your-core-group/growing-your-core-group) lists people who are unhappy with their current church among contacts you may already know. Unhappiness is not permission to work that congregation as a prospect list. If you mean to invite several of those people because they belong there, agree on sending first. If one of them asks you, hear them. That request is not a campaign.

[Invitation Strategies](/wiki/core-group/vision-meetings/invitation-strategies) still covers the invitation itself. Be direct. Accept a no. Do not criticize another church. Do not pressure. This article adds one prior step for one kind of list. It does not add a pastoral release to every personal invitation, and it does not take back the counsel to use former church connections.

---

## Ask for sending, not for a roster

Ask for a shared purpose before you ask for people.

- Say where you are planting and what you hope they will consider.
- Ask whether they will send members with you, and on what terms.
- Ask who should invite, what the congregation will be told, and when.
- Agree that a no ends targeted invitations to their members.
- Leave with a clear yes, a clear no, or a date to decide. A warm tone is not an agreement.

Do not open with the members you want. Do not describe who is frustrated, who gives, or who would be useful on a Launch Team. You can ask whether the church will send people without naming one of them.

The Launch Playbook tells you to use mailing lists sparingly, and only with your coach's prior permission. That permission is a conversation with your coach. It is not a control in Everyfield, and it is not a reason to request another church's list.

<Callout type="tip">
Use a plain ask. "We want to invite people from your congregation only if you are sending them with us. If you would rather we not, we will not target your members. Can we talk about what sending would look like?"
</Callout>

---

## Leave their story with them

You may know why a person is restless. That knowledge is not yours to trade. Do not tell their pastor the complaint, the family situation, or the giving pattern unless that person has agreed to the words you will use.

If the leaders are willing to send, let them tell their own people, or invite only the people you have both agreed to approach. If a person later wants their pastor told, they can say so, or they can sit in the conversation with you. Do not widen that yes into permission to invite their small group.

A comment from their pastor is not the fit interview. Fit is still a human conversation on Maturity, Gifted, Chemistry, Right Reasons, and Season of Life. Record that result the way you already do. Do not write the other pastor's yes or no in its place. [Interviewing for Fit](/wiki/core-group/follow-up/interviewing-for-fit) and [The 5 Interview Criteria](/wiki/frameworks/the-5-interview-criteria) are the path for that decision.

---

## When someone asks you first

A friend writes after hearing about the plant. A guest stays after a Vision Meeting and asks what joining would mean. Hear them. Invite them if they want to come, and follow up as you would with any guest. You do not need a sending agreement before you will talk with someone who asked.

You may ask whether they want you to speak with their pastor. If they say no, do not make that call the price of the conversation. If they say yes, agree on the words, then say only those words. One person's yes is not cover for a list, and their pastor does not get a veto over the move.

If they and their church are already in a dispute, do not invent a ruling from this page. Say what you can decide and what you cannot. A human works the case. Software will not score it.

<Callout type="warning">
If someone reports harm, coercion, or a reason they cannot safely have their pastor contacted, do not pass their account to that church as part of recruitment. Do not require pastoral contact before you will listen. This guide is not a script for abuse, legal duty, or church discipline.
</Callout>

---

## If the leaders say no

Thank them. Stop targeting their members. Tell your Core Group the boundary in plain words, so a helpful member does not keep inviting "just a few."

A no is not a reason to criticize that church. Do not explain the refusal by ranking their pastor, their people, or your plant. People who come from another congregation and people who come to faith are different stories. Notice the difference so you can tell the truth about the work. Do not treat a transfer as a lesser member, or as a number to chase.

If a person from that church later asks you on their own, hear them. A no to your campaign is not a ban on an individual. It is a ban on you going after the membership.

---

## Before you invite their members

Use this list when a congregation is in view. Skip it when the person has already asked you and there is no list behind them.

- [ ] Name the congregation and the leader who can speak for it.
- [ ] Pause invitations to its current members, including casual ones from your Core Group.
- [ ] Ask for a sending arrangement before you collect or use names.
- [ ] Agree who invites, what will be said, and what a no means.
- [ ] Keep private stories out of that meeting unless the person has agreed to the words.
- [ ] If the leaders decline, tell the Core Group to stop targeting those members.
- [ ] If someone asks on their own, hear them without turning their friends into a list.
- [ ] Leave fit to the human interview. Do not record another pastor's opinion as the result.

---

<Callout type="scripture">
*"Then, when they had fasted and prayed and laid their hands on them, they sent them away."* — Acts 13:3 (LSB)
</Callout>

They fasted, prayed, laid hands on them, and sent them away. Ask for that kind of sending before you invite another congregation's members. When a person comes to you on their own, receive them. Do not pretend their pastor holds the key to their going.

Wording: title is "Agree on Sending Before You Recruit" because it states Option B more plainly than the backlog title. Slug stays the brief's suggested slug.

Wording: the new step applies only to planned recruitment of a congregation's current members. Independent asks and former connections stay on the published invitation path, so this article does not add a pastoral release to every personal invitation.
Wording: dissatisfaction named in Growing Your Core Group is not a license to target that church's members before a sending agreement, and it is not a reason to refuse someone who asks on their own.

Wording: this article makes no theological claim that a pastor may permit or refuse someone's departure. Unsafe or disputed cases are handled by a person, not routed through the other church as a recruitment step, and not scored by software.
